_meta.description: Ten cast entries for the twenty-five-chapter campaign, with pronouns, acts and the speaking rules.

pronoun_policy: Lancer Ivanov has no pronouns and never speaks. Other people have their pronouns recorded here; organizational voices and recorded designations use null. I kept the rule in one place so the cast file is the only thing that has to change.

characters.note: A surface courier in the twenties or thirties. Lancer never speaks, so every attached line is a bracketed action direction. I don't use pronouns or gendered voice direction for Lancer in any locale.

The prequel protagonist and the Concord's FIRST RUNNER. A veteran smuggler who trained Lancer, Ilsa spent the Fracture Year as a military dispatch runner. She survived the Concord's drop and cut the first illegal routes across the walls. Ilsa says nothing in the five prequel chapters. In the present day she talks, and what she says is usually a route.

Human containment enforcement. Saye is a young logistics officer in the prequel, watching the war spiral out of control. Twenty years later, she is the exhausted administrator who signed the isolation accords. She talks at Lancer across checkpoints and security glass. Lancer never answers.
The siege organism itself. It speaks through street displays, PA chimes and containment logs. There is no face and no ego behind the voice.

The Concord gives this tag to Ilsa Renn's recorded movement profile from the Fracture Year. It has run simulations of the route ever since, using them to hunt modern couriers. It is a recording of her, not a separate person.

Lead biomechanical containment researcher at the Longhorn Biological Facility. In the Fracture Year, he gives Ilsa Renn the facility's master override key during the drop. Twenty years later, Lancer finds his audio logs, then finds Thorne still alive inside the expanded Concord Monolith.

He is an exhausted infantry squad leader holding the perimeter around Central Station and the Longhorn Facility while Ilsa runs encryption keys through active warzones. Miller appears in the prequel only, chapters P1 to P3.

He is an underground block machinist in Quarantine Block 404 and a former Wind Regulator technician. Henrik maintains Lancer's Filament tether, repairs salvaged rifles and assembles the L-01 Arc-Lance from regulator parts.
She is a signal operator for the Free-Band Network. Talia links shortwave transmitters across the Block Seam and feeds Lancer tactical intel over a one-way earpiece. Lancer stays silent.
The civil-defence broadcasts of the Fracture Year. A channel with a voice on it and nobody behind it, and the last thing Lancer hears before the Concord takes the sky.
